title: Roasted dandelion root brew
subtitle: A bitter digestive drink of roasted Taraxacum officinale root, a caffeine-free coffee substitute
excerpt: Roasted dandelion root brew is made from oven-dried and roasted dandelion root, simmered for 10 minutes and strained into a mug. It has the colour, weight, and mild bitterness of weak coffee without the caffeine, and has been used in herbal practice as a digestive bitter to stimulate bile flow and support sluggish digestion before or after meals. Makes one cup per session. Roasted root stores 6 months in a sealed jar.
sourceNotes: Maud Grieve, A Modern Herbal (1931), dandelion entry, Botanical.com. EMA HMPC Community herbal monograph on Taraxacum officinale Weber ex F.H.Wigg., radix cum herba (2009), open access. Roasted dandelion root as a coffee substitute: documented wartime use in UK, Germany, and France during WWII; botanical recipe sources pre-1930.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Roasted dandelion root stores 6 months in a sealed jar, roast in batches and use as needed.

glossaryTerms.definition: A herb with an intensely bitter taste that stimulates the secretion of digestive juices, saliva, stomach acid, and bile, when tasted. Bitter herbs activate receptors on the tongue and in the gut lining that trigger the digestive cascade. Dandelion root is a mild, reliable digestive bitter.

content.text: Roasted dandelion root brew is made by simmering 1 teaspoon of roasted, chopped Taraxacum officinale root in 200 ml of water for 10 minutes, then straining into a mug. It has the weight and colour of weak coffee without any caffeine. A traditional

, taken before or after meals to stimulate bile flow and support sluggish digestion. Widely used in wartime Europe as a coffee substitute when supplies were scarce, and carried into post-war herbal practice. The roasting process creates the brown colour and mellows the raw bitterness of the fresh root. The brew has a pleasantly earthy, slightly bitter flavour, best drunk black without sugar.

attrs.title: Precautions
attrs.body: Not medical advice. Consult a qualified herbalist or doctor before use. Full precautions are in the 'When not to use' section.

items.prepNote: roasted, dried dandelion root, chop or grind to coarse pieces before roasting

content.text: To roast the root: spread chopped dried dandelion root in a single layer on a baking tray. Roast at 180 °C for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring halfway, until the pieces are deep brown and smell of roasted chicory. Allow to cool, then store in a sealed jar.
To brew: place 1 teaspoon of roasted root in a small saucepan with 250 ml of cold water. Bring to a simmer and simmer gently for 10 minutes.
Strain through a fine strainer into a mug. Drink black before or after a meal. A small amount of oat milk softens the bitterness without destroying the digestive action.
One cup before or after meals, up to twice daily. For sluggish digestion, taken consistently for 4 weeks before assessing the effect.
Roasted dandelion root stores 6 months in a sealed jar at room temperature. Brew fresh each time.
When not to use this remedy
Avoid if you have a known Asteraceae allergy or active gallstones. See a doctor for persistent digestive symptoms, significant unexplained weight loss, or jaundice.
